notes: Circuit: 5V -> pushbutton (column 8) ; pin 4 -> pushbutton (column 6) with 10k pull-down resistor from column 6 (pin 4 node) to GND rail. Matches the manual text; the schematic drawing shows pin 2 but the manual text and breadboard image use pin 4, so pin 4 is used.

Breadboard hole positions are estimated from the image: black GND wire at bn.2, red 5V wire at bp.3, resistor lower lead at bn.6, button legs in columns 6 and 8 straddling the centre gap, blue wire at 6t.c, short red wire from 8t.c to bp.8. The picture's rows f-j are shown at the top, but the catalogue names the rows a-e half 't' and f-j half 'b', so button legs are 6t.e/8t.e and 6b.f/8b.f.
The two button legs in the same column are treated as one side (1 = column 6, 2 = column 8), per the catalogue pushbutton note.
The Leonardo's USB cable to the computer is mentioned in the text but is not part of the wired circuit, so it is not included.
Rail polarity: the rail row next to the black line is treated as negative (bn) and the row next to the red line as positive (bp).
The Leonardo's first GND pin (highlighted in the image) is mapped to GND.1.
